title: Quantifiers: Groups and Parts
summary: Use all, most, some, any, no and none to describe whole groups, parts of groups and zero quantities. Choose the correct form when you name a general group or a particular group.
learningObjectives: Use all, most and some directly before a noun to describe people or things in general.
Add of where necessary when a quantifier refers to a defined group.
Distinguish no before a noun from none of before a specific group.
Use quantifier + of + object pronoun to refer back to people or things.

explanation.heading: Talk about things in general
explanation.body: When you mean a general group, use all, most or some directly before a plural noun or an uncountable noun. Do not insert of before a noun with no determiner. For example, most visitors refers to visitors generally, not to a particular set.
explanation.example: Most gardens need water in summer.

explanation.heading: Talk about a particular group
explanation.body: Use most of, some of or any of before the, this, these, my and similar words. These expressions select people or things from a group you can identify. The form is quantifier + of + determiner + noun.
explanation.example: Some of my classmates walk to school.

explanation.heading: Use all with or without of
explanation.body: With a defined group, all the and all of the have the same basic meaning. All my neighbours and all of my neighbours are both possible. With a general plural noun, use all without of.
explanation.example: All of the windows in our flat face the garden.

explanation.heading: Express zero with no, none and not any
explanation.body: Use no directly before a noun: no tickets. Use none of before a defined group: none of these tickets. In standard English, a negative verb normally takes any, not no: I do not have any tickets. None can also stand alone as a short answer.
explanation.example: None of the cups on this shelf is clean.

explanation.heading: Refer back with of + pronoun
explanation.body: After all, most, some, any or none, use of before it, them, us or you. Use them for a plural group and it for an uncountable amount or one thing. Do not say most them or none us.
explanation.example: I invited six friends, and most of them came.

left.label: General
left.example: Most travellers carry a small bag.
left.note: No of before travellers when speaking generally.

right.label: Particular
right.example: Most of our travellers arrived early.
right.note: Use of before our to select a known group.

comparisons.title: No before a noun; none of before a group

left.label: No + noun
left.note: No comes directly before the noun phrase.

right.label: None of + group
right.example: None of these towels is clean.
right.note: None of refers to a defined set of towels.

examples.sentence: Some cafés open early on Sundays.
examples.note: Some describes part of a general group.

examples.sentence: Most of the seats near the window are free.
examples.note: Of the identifies the seats being discussed.
All can precede a possessive directly.

examples.sentence: I have not used any of these plates.
examples.note: Any of refers to items in a particular group in a negative sentence.

examples.sentence: We bought three oranges and ate all of them.
examples.note: Of them replaces a previously mentioned plural noun.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Most of tourists carry a camera.
commonMistakes.why: Leave out of when the plural noun describes people generally.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Some my neighbours work at night.
commonMistakes.correct: Some of my neighbours work at night.
commonMistakes.why: Use of between some and the possessive my.

commonMistakes.incorrect: No of these apples is ripe.
commonMistakes.correct: None of these apples is ripe.
commonMistakes.why: Use none of, not no of, before a defined group.

commonMistakes.incorrect: I do not have no free time.
commonMistakes.correct: I do not have any free time.
commonMistakes.why: In standard negative sentences, not pairs with any; no is used without not.

studyTips: Look at the word after the quantifier: a bare noun usually takes no of; the, these or my usually calls for of after most, some or any.
Practise the pairs no + noun and none of + group. Say a full sentence for each pair.
When replacing a group with a pronoun, remember the of: some of it, most of them, none of us.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct beginning: ___ musicians practise regularly.
exercises.feedback: Most + a bare plural noun describes musicians in general.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: ___ my cousins live nearby.
exercises.feedback: Most of is required before a possessive such as my.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: There is not ___ juice in the fridge.
exercises.feedback: Not any is the normal standard negative form before an uncountable noun.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: ___ the postcards on this table are from Italy.
exercises.feedback: Some of the refers to a specific collection of postcards.

exercises.prompt: Complete with 'none' or 'no': ___ of these postcards belongs to me; they all belong to Eva.
acceptedAnswers: None
exercises.feedback: None of is used for zero items in a defined group.

exercises.prompt: Complete with 'no' or 'none': We have ___ clean glasses, so please wash a few.
acceptedAnswers: no
exercises.feedback: No goes directly before the noun phrase clean glasses.

exercises.prompt: Complete with 'some' or 'some of': ___ of us are going by train; the others are driving.
acceptedAnswers: Some
exercises.feedback: Some of us means a part of our group.

exercises.prompt: Complete with 'most' or 'most of': ___ the tables in the café are occupied.
acceptedAnswers: Most of
exercises.feedback: The identifies a particular set of tables, so use most of.

exercises.prompt: Remove the unnecessary word: Most of tourists visit the market.
acceptedAnswers: Most tourists visit the market.
exercises.feedback: Most goes directly before a plural noun that represents people in general.

exercises.prompt: Add the missing word: Some my colleagues cycle to work.
acceptedAnswers: Some of my colleagues cycle to work.
exercises.feedback: Use some of before the possessive my.

exercises.prompt: Replace the incorrect quantifier: No of these rooms has a balcony.
acceptedAnswers: None of these rooms has a balcony.
exercises.feedback: None of, not no of, means zero within a specific set.

exercises.prompt: Replace only the incorrect quantifier: I don't have no clean socks.
acceptedAnswers: I don't have any clean socks.
exercises.feedback: After do not, use any before the noun in standard English.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say the completed sentence aloud, using 'Most': '___ dogs enjoy a walk.'
acceptedAnswers: Most dogs enjoy a walk.
speakingExercises.feedback: Most goes directly before the general plural noun dogs.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say one sentence starting 'None of the bags ...': There are three bags, and zero belong to Nina.
acceptedAnswers: None of the bags belongs to Nina.
None of the bags belong to Nina.
speakingExercises.feedback: None of identifies zero items from the three bags; both singular and plural agreement occur in usage.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say the completed sentence aloud, including 'all of': 'We finished ___ the work.'
acceptedAnswers: We finished all of the work.
speakingExercises.feedback: All of the refers to the complete amount of a specific task.

speakingExercises.prompt: In a box of five notebooks, two have labels and three do not. Say one complete sentence beginning "Some of the notebooks" and ending "have labels".
acceptedAnswers: Some of the notebooks have labels.
speakingExercises.feedback: Some of the identifies part of a particular group of notebooks. The plural subject takes have.

speakingExercises.prompt: Rewrite "There are no blue plates in this box" using "None of the plates" and the plural verb "are". Keep the place and colour.
acceptedAnswers: None of the plates in this box are blue.
speakingExercises.feedback: None of the plates identifies zero blue plates in the specific group. Use none of, not no of.

speakingExercises.prompt: You ate part of the cake Mia brought, but not the whole cake. Tell Mia what you ate. Begin "I ate" and use "some of the cake".
acceptedAnswers: I ate some of the cake.
speakingExercises.feedback: Some of the refers to part of a particular cake. The article the makes the group specific.

speakingExercises.prompt: Correct this sentence and say it aloud: "I invited eight friends, and most them came." Change only what is necessary.
acceptedAnswers: I invited eight friends, and most of them came.
speakingExercises.feedback: A quantifier followed by the object pronoun them needs of: most of them.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say exactly two short sentences. First: "I bought four peaches." Then say that two are ripe, beginning "Some of them" and ending "are ripe".
acceptedAnswers: I bought four peaches. Some of them are ripe.
speakingExercises.feedback: Some of them refers back to part of the group of four peaches, without repeating the noun.

listeningExercises.audioText: Most of the shops on this street close at six.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which group does the speaker describe?
listeningExercises.feedback: Most of the shops on this street refers to a particular local group.

listeningExercises.audioText: None of our chairs is broken.
listeningExercises.prompt: How many of the chairs are broken?
listeningExercises.feedback: None of our chairs means not one chair in that group.

listeningExercises.audioText: I have no spare batteries at home.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the one word immediately before “spare batteries” in the audio.
acceptedAnswers: no
listeningExercises.feedback: No directly before a noun phrase expresses zero quantity.

listeningExercises.audioText: All the bedrooms in our guest house have large windows.
listeningExercises.prompt: What can a guest expect in any bedroom?
choices: A window only in the largest bedroom.
A large window in every bedroom.
listeningExercises.feedback: All the bedrooms describes the whole specific group, so no bedroom is without a large window.

listeningExercises.audioText: I checked eight lanterns, and most of them still work.
listeningExercises.prompt: How many of the checked items are still working?
listeningExercises.feedback: Most of them means a majority of the eight lanterns, so more than four still work.

listeningExercises.audioText: I bought five greeting cards, but I did not send any of them.
listeningExercises.feedback: Did not send any of them means zero cards in that particular group were sent.

listeningExercises.audioText: Some of those hikers are still on the mountain.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word quantifier immediately before "those hikers".
acceptedAnswers: some of
listeningExercises.feedback: Some of introduces a part of a specified group: those hikers.

listeningExercises.audioText: We had four sandwiches and ate all of them before noon.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the three-word expression indicating the entire group was eaten.
acceptedAnswers: all of them
listeningExercises.feedback: All of them means the complete previously mentioned group of sandwiches.
